title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. L(t) is a rational function in t, with q = p^f. Context: the L-function of a curve or of an l-adic sheaf over F_q, in the self-dual case. It satisfies a functional equation L(1/(qt)) = A(t) L(t), where A(t) is a simple correction factor. In the classical case of a curve of genus g, L = P(t) and A(t) = q^{-g} t^{-2g}; in general A is roughly epsilon·(monomial).

The problem. Grothendieck wants to renormalise L' = λ L, with λ rational, so that the functional equation becomes pure: L'(1/(qt)) = c L'(t) with c a constant.

The computation. Write σ for the involution t ↦ 1/(qt).
- L'(σt) = λ(σt) A(t) L(t) = λ(σt) λ(t)^{-1} A(t) L'(t).
- So the condition is λ(σt)/λ(t) = c A(t)^{-1}.
- If λ is one solution, any other λ' = αλ (with constant c') satisfies α(σt)/α(t) = c'/c =: a.
- Since σ² = id, applying the relation twice gives a² = 1, so a = ±1. Hence the constant c of the simplified equation is determined up to sign.

Reformulation. Grothendieck then lets Z/2Z act on the nonzero rational functions K(t)^* via σ. He starts to phrase the question, for given c, as finding λ, i.e. as a question in group cohomology H^1(Z/2, K(t)^*).

Modern completion.
- Since L(t) = A(σt) A(t) L(t), A satisfies the cocycle condition A·σ(A) = 1.
- The modified cocycle c A^{-1} is again a cocycle exactly when c² = 1.
- K(t)/K(t)^σ = K(t)/K(u), with u = t + 1/(qt), is a quadratic Galois extension. Hilbert 90 gives H^1(Z/2, K(t)^*) = 0, so λ always exists for c = 1 and also for c = -1.
- The sign flip is realised by α = t - 1/(qt), which satisfies α(σt) = -α(t).
- For a curve, λ = t^{-g} gives L' = t^{-g} P(t) with L'(1/(qt)) = L'(t).

Purpose. This is a preliminary normalisation, the analogue of completing ζ to a symmetric Λ-function. It feeds into the study of the functional equation and of the epsilon/root-number sign in the geometric case of cote 60.
errors: Not an error but a gap: the conclusion 'c is determined up to sign' is weaker than what actually holds. Applying the simplified equation twice already forces c² = 1. Moreover, with λ allowed to be an arbitrary rational function, both signs are realisable: α = t - 1/(qt) is anti-invariant, so multiplying λ by it flips c. By Hilbert 90 for K(t)/K(t)^σ a solution λ always exists. So the sign c (root number) carries no invariant information unless λ is restricted, e.g. to monomials c·t^{n/2} or to functions without zeros or poles away from 0 and ∞. The page breaks off before addressing this.
The cocycle condition A(t)A(1/(qt)) = 1, needed for solvability, is not stated on this page, though it follows immediately from the functional equation.

ideas.what: Renormalising an L-function by a rational factor to make its functional equation symmetric under t ↦ 1/(qt)
ideas.modern_name: Completed / symmetric L-function, e.g. t^{-g}P(t) for curves; normalisation of the functional equation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Weil, Artin; analogue of the completed zeta function)
ideas.where_published: The functional equation of L-functions is treated in SGA 5 (Grothendieck's exposé on the Lefschetz–Verdier formula and L-functions) and later in Deligne's 'Les constantes des équations fonctionnelles des fonctions L'; this specific normalisation computation is not known to be published.

ideas.what: Viewing the existence of the normalising factor λ as a cohomology problem for Z/2 acting on K(t)^* by t ↦ 1/(qt)
Ambiguity of the constant c up to sign under change of normalisation
ideas.modern_name: Root number / epsilon-factor sign; dependence on normalisation

deep.surprise_reason: This is an elementary scratch computation normalising the functional equation of a rational L-function, i.e. Hilbert 90 for a Z/2 action on K(t)^*. It is routine and well known. Its main interest is as a trace of Grothendieck's work on the geometric functional equation and epsilon constants, and nothing new appears.
